reviews.author: m c
reviews.text: This place exemplifies so many amazing state parks that Washington state has to offer! It's on the water so you can drive in or boat in with a boat dock to tie up and mooring balls. No power or water but Port Townsend's just a hop away. Some great world war II history and wonderful landscape.

reviews.author: Jeremy Botkin
reviews.text: This is a premier State Park. Beautiful views, adventurous hiking trails and historical sites. Plenty of beaches and a boat ramp and dock. Excellent kayaking waters and tons of nature to enjoy. In the summer season the snack shack has yummy soft serve ice cream and other delights.

reviews.author: Rhodes family
reviews.text: Beautiful trails along the coast and through the woods. Plus you get to explore some historical bunkers, artillery rooms etc. Super windy the closer you get to the coastal trail. Make sure to pack a windbreaker and/or something warm. If you want to explore all the military bunkers, highly recommend to bring a flashlight. Your cellphone flashlight just won’t cut it.

reviews.author: K Seale
reviews.text:
This Washington State Park campground was a 5-star stay! The trails connecting the campground to the historical batteries and Fort are well-maintained; I didn't even need my hiking poles (even though it was muddy). They would be helpful, however, for seniors like myself hiking some of the smaller trails traversing over tree roots - like the narrow one that's parallel to the road that goes from Fort to the campground.
At the broadest expanse of batteries, I watched at least 6 eagles in the skies overhead while 2 perched on their lookout. What an experience for this nature lover! Also enjoyed the daffodils, harbor seals (over 20), the "seashell ornament" trees, Port Townsend lit up at night across the bay, and Olympic Mountain views.
We arrived with an engine problem in our diesel truck and a CG employee recommended a mobile mechanic. We were able to extend our reservation by 2 days and it got fixed!
This is a repeat visit; we'll be back!

reviews.author: Tammy French
reviews.text: Amazing historical park overlooking the sea across from Whidbey Island. It is a military installated from the 1850s pretty much. Many generations and iterations of the fort. Beautiful natural surroundings. Well maintained historical areas and lodging.

reviews.title: Wonderful gem in my own backyard. Great views and good hiking.
reviews.author: camp-roadtripper833935
reviews.text: Amazingly, we never stayed at Fort Flagler SP, even though we can see it from our home in Port Townsend. Why did we wait so long? We stayed on the lower campground loop, adjacent to the beach with water views on two sides. The sites are very spacious and composed of grass covered pebbles. Very solid and level. Sites are 50amp F/H with great water pressure. Unfortunately, the sites are not oriented so that we could point the big windshield towards the water. A very small annoyance. Did not use the shower or restroom facilities. There's a lot of woodland hiking around the forts artillery batteries. The park was kept exceptionally clean, with dumpsters and recycling close by. The lower campground does have WiFi that ran at about 7 - 9Mbps download. Plenty for web surfing, Facebook and emailing. The entrance road is narrow, causing big rigs to drive partially on the grass shoulder in order to pass by each other. Bring your own food, as there is no grocery on Marrowstone Island. Will definitely return!

reviews.title: Easy To Get A Spot Day After Thanksgiving
reviews.author: camper-896912
reviews.text: Other campgrounds in the area were full, but there were a number of open spots here the day after Thanksgiving! $20 / night for the non-hookup spots. Heated flushing bathrooms! Nice beach at the lower campground too.

reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.author: Travel Small Live Big!
reviews.text: We stayed here for 2 nights late September in 2024. Just got lucky & could get a site for 2 nights, one of which was a Friday! Nice site - long enough and it worked. I thought the price was ok for FHU. The view & sunsets were stunning and it was a great spot to park to visit Port Townsend. I wished I could have reserved the site for longer... next time!

reviews.author: EdgarH
reviews.text: Great place if you can get a place near the water. Very good Wi-Fi and reception. Great view to Port Townsend.

reviews.author: A-Simple-Change-of-View
reviews.text: Since the reservation system does not allow same day reservations, we showed up hoping to grab one of the few available sights as first come, first served. There were 3 or 4 sites listed as available in the lower campground and we found one that was perfect for us. We had the choice between a full hook up site and a dry site and chose the latter as it was perfectly level and offered more privacy. It’s interesting to note the different pricing levels from ‘popular’ to basic. Some sites were tightly packed and others were absolutely enormous with great views. Our site, 105, had a very tight neighboring spot on just one side (a no show which gave us a much roomier feeling) and an ample area with picnic table, fire pit, and enough room for two tents behind the pad. A short trail, albeit somewhat overgrown, at the back of our site lead right to the beach. The campground, while quite full, was incredibly quiet. I’m sure things are different in the summer time with more families camping. The hosts and maintenance folks were all very friendly. Perhaps my favorite part of this campground is the location with miles of beach to walk. I was surprised that with our frequent strolls on the beach with the pups, we only passed a small number of people. The dump station worked as expected and had potable water available.

reviews.author: Silver-Streaker
reviews.text: It is a great place to take the family. Nice balance of activities, facilities, and views. Still popular and well maintained as of June 2022. Note on T-Mobile cell service: I think the antenna may be at Port Townsend, so there is a great signal across the water when at the campground and the museum area. Some places of the island were dead zones.

reviews.author: kjwithers
reviews.text: My happy place! Great hikes, good beaches and close to Pt. Townsend. Quiet and safe.

reviews.author: David Williamson
reviews.text: I've been taking my son to Fort Flagler for several years now. We go once or twice a year. It is the perfect campground for kids. It has 2 main camping areas, lower and upper. Lower campground is better suited in general for RVs. It has little tree cover and there is more wind down there. Upper campground has heavy tree cover which keeps your site and tent cool during the day. There is a general store on site that sells firewood, ice cream, burgers/hotdogs/etc, kites, canned food, drinks, and lots more. It is a great resource. Nearby is a kids playground too. Around this area is plenty of open space which is perfect for kite flying. There is plenty of beach to comb, some on the Kilisut Harbor side, and some in the Admiralty Inlet. Kilisut Harbor is cold, but protected and is a pretty good option for boating/kayaking. One of this campgrounds best features are the trails, suitable for hiking and bicycling. On these trails you'll see deer, and they lead to amazing views of the surrounding areas. What's more, there are WW1 and WW2 bunkers and batteries to check out, which my kid just loves. Bicycling is probably our favorite activity when camping here. A day trip to Port Townsend is nice. Be sure to stop by for ice cream at Elevated Ice Cream Co & Candy Shop. I highly recommend the orange and swiss chocolate flavor. For many people, driving to Fort Flagler involves a ferry ride, which is a nice part of the trip too. The only downside I've ever experienced is loud noises at night from something outside the campground. We're not sure if it is wind on the cliffs or planes from military exercises. We don't hear it every stay, and never two nights in a row.

reviews.author: Emma62
reviews.text: Nice view, entrance was closed, need to look for empty space on the list, nice people supporting. I recommend this place.

reviews.author: Sayler09
reviews.text: Great place for kids to ride bicycles and enjoy the Day by the water and trees

Lower loop is pretty fantastic, especially along the waterfront. Sites are generous and the campground itself was clean and plenty quiet (no loud neighbors!). We saw wildlife galore- bald eagles, seals, fish jumping, deer wandering the beach… spectacular! Sunsets were gorgeous too! If there’s any downside at all, it might be that groceries are a solid 20m drive one way to get, but that’s no fault of the campground, it’s a trade-off for the location. Edited to add: we have Verizon and had great reception in the lower loop. Service goes out in the wooded areas and several times in the last 20 mins of the drive or so, but otherwise we had no issues calling or using data.
reviews.date: Month of Visit: August (year not shown)

reviews.text: We stayed here as a base to go whale watching out of Port Townsend. We really liked the campground, but it's a bit excluded, out on the end of the island. It takes a while to drive over to Port Townsend - and anywhere, really. That said, it's beautiful and we really liked it. We didn't get a chance to explore the trails or much of the base, but we'd love to go back sometime. We stayed in the upper campground, in the trees. The views are nice on the beach, but we prefer a little more privacy. The showers require tokens and didn't work all the time.
reviews.date: Month of Visit: June (year not shown)
